label: D2 after a1 -> S1 (common), late in the episode (trial >= ~80)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a1 and the common transition took it to S1 (in_action=1, in_state=1). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a2, or when S1 was reached by a rare a2 transition or S2 by a rare a1 transition. It is also strongly gated by time in the episode: silent before trial ~70, onset around trials 70-79, and most of its activation mass falls in trials 80-99. Within a window, magnitude rises steadily with trial index (e.g. 0.47 -> 0.54 -> 0.60 -> 0.65 -> 0.70 over consecutive a1->S1 trials), and value-head output is low when it fires. The previous or upcoming reward has little effect on whether it fires. Without the time condition the a1->S1 D2 predicate has recall 1.0 but precision 0.20. Adding ep_trial >= 80 gives dev F1 0.92 and mass recall 0.99; most misses are weak activations at trials 70-79. ep_trial is not an input, so the agent must track elapsed time internally. The predicate uses only observed inputs plus episode position, so no future variables.

issues: Every factual claim checked out. On dev, the feature is active on 0 D1 and 0 GO steps. In_action=2, in_state=2 and rare transitions all have 0 active steps. Nothing fires before trial 60 and there is 1 activation in trials 60-69. Trials 70-79 hold 1% of the activation mass, 80-89 hold 25% and 90-99 hold 74%. All activity falls in the two lowest value-head bins.

On test, the predicate scores P 0.924, R 0.923, F1 0.924, mass recall 0.992, which reproduces the reported numbers. Outside the a1->S1 D2 condition at trials >= 80 there is essentially no activity (1 active step out of 54,908).

Test misses: 1946 steps holding 0.8% of the mass. Almost all of them are weak activations at trials 70-79 (the a1->S1 D2 steps at trials 70-79 cover 1945 active steps, with precision 0.14). This matches the explanation.

False positives are not scattered noise, but they sit only at the weak edges of the feature. Precision is 0.77 at trials 80-84 against 0.998 at trials >= 90, which is the gradual time onset. It is 0.65 on the first a1->S1 trial after an a2 choice, against 0.95 when the previous choice was also a1, which fits the claim that magnitude builds over consecutive a1 trials. The two classes overlap heavily. Excluding the overlap (prev_action == 2 at trials 80-84) raises test F1 only to 0.931 (P 0.941, R 0.922), so neither class counts as a systematic counterexample.

Rewards matter little within the predicate. Precision is 0.94 vs 0.90 for previous reward 1 vs 0, and 0.94 vs 0.91 for this trial's reward 1 vs 0, so a predicate on the observed variables alone explains the feature. The predicate uses no future variables.

Minor nit: one way of splitting by start_high flips between splits (dev mass 77% start_high=0, test 78% start_high=1). This most likely reflects which reversals happen to fall late in the episode, not a property of the feature, and the label does not claim anything about it.
